reason_investigated: Examine discrete vs. continuous shear connection modeling and effective flexural rigidity bounds.
model: Comparison between Newmark's continuous differential method and Kamiya's discrete recurrence difference equation method.
method: Comparison between rigorous recurrence difference equations and continuous differential equations.
experiment: Numerical validation comparing discrete recurrence formulations with continuous Newmark solutions.
parameter_domain: Two-layer beams with discrete flexible connectors under small deflections.
breakdown_assessment: MODEL_BREAKDOWN_STUDIED (analyzes error of continuous smeared models when connector pitch is large).

title: Theoretical, experimental, and numerical simulation studies on interface slip in steel-concrete composite continuous beams with high-strength bolted connectors
repository_path: data/inbox/verification_pending/D1-V006/C03_imperfect_interface/2025-Theoretical, experimental, and numerical simulation studies on interface slip in steel-concrete.pdf
reason_investigated: Audited in C03 to determine whether analytical interface slip models of continuous beams establish validity limits or breakdown boundaries.
model: Analytical second-order differential equation for interface slip and slip-induced deflection.
method: Benchmarking analytical slip model against 3D Abaqus solid contact FEA and experimental test data.
experiment: Full-scale physical test on a 7.2 m two-span continuous composite beam using hydraulic actuator.

parameter_domain.structure: 2-span continuous composite beam (2 layers: steel + concrete)
parameter_domain.load_range: 0 to 600 kN static loading (elastic and ultimate)

outputs: interface slip s(x) measured by LVDTs

error_metrics.validity_metric: Relative error in interfacial slip distribution and beam deflection vs 3D FEA
error_metrics.validity_threshold: None declared; curve-fit comparison in elastic stage
error_metrics.model_form_error_metric: Peak slip difference 2.03% to 2.09% vs 3D FEA; deflection error 0.77% to 2.71% in elastic service stage

breakdown_assessment: Explicitly demonstrates breakdown of the elastic slip model when concrete cracking and bolt yielding initiate.
higher_fidelity_reference: 3D nonlinear Abaqus solid contact FE model.
reference_resolution_level: 3D solid elements resolving concrete slab, steel girder, and individual bolted connectors.
failure_mechanism_analysis: Concrete negative moment cracking and bolt plastic shear yielding violating linear slip assumptions.
what_it_proves: Second-order analytical interface slip equations match 3D solid contact FEA within 2–3% in the elastic regime, but break down when material nonlinearity and plastic slip occur.
what_it_does_not_prove: Only 2 layers (steel girder + concrete slab); does not address N-layer contact, vacuum jamming, friction-dominated locking, or predeclared breakdown boundaries.
impact_on_D1: Demonstrates successful execution of an M->R->E workflow for 2-layer composite beams, leaving N-layer vacuum jamming open.
